column1: # tools/css/gen-cssom-tables.py: what CSSOM does with each kind of rule (css_cssom_rule.h). One row for each of the kinds of css_atrule.h (the at-rule enumeration,
# UNKNOWN included) and for the two that are not at-rules, the style rule and the nested-declarations rule: 29 rows. The at-rules' rows are checked against
# tools/css/atrule_kinds.tsv (every kind of its ledger has a row, every row that is not in the ledger is one of the kinds the parse itself makes), and the places a
# rule may be (its `parents` column) are taken from there, not written twice. Tab separated:
#  kind        the name gtext_css_atrule_kind_name() gives, or `style` or `nested-declarations`
#  interface   the CSSOM interface(s), `-` for none (no browser exposes the kind, or it is not a rule)
#  type        the legacy `type` constant CSSOM lists for the rule (0 for every newer one)
#  list        what its cssRules holds: none, rules (style, nested-declarations and at-rules), keyframes, margins
#  style       what its `style` is: none, properties (a block of property declarations), descriptors (a block of descriptors)
#  rule        yes: a parse makes a rule object of it (a keyframe and a margin rule only inside their parent). no: never a rule object
#  insertable  yes: insertRule can make one at the top level or in a group
